subject: zoology_2
question_text: What is a 'motor unit' with reference to muscle and nerve?

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.50, VSAQ 78. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Text revision (examiner audit, 2026-09-05): step 2's why and margin note now state that one motor neuron supplies many fibres, so they match the step's mark label and its listed mistake; the printed line was left as it stands because it is correct.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The neuron
steps.why: One motor neuron carries one command, so everything it reaches must contract together.
common_mistakes: Naming a sensory neuron. A motor unit uses a motor neuron.
steps.memory_tip: One nerve cell plus everything it commands.
steps.margin_note: Definition in one sentence, but say both halves.
lines: A motor unit is a motor neuron together
with the muscle fibres it supplies.

steps.label: The fibres it supplies
steps.why: One motor neuron supplies many muscle fibres, because the fine branches of its axon, the telodendrites, end on all of them at once, so a single signal moves them together.
common_mistakes: Writing that one neuron supplies one fibre. It supplies many.
steps.memory_tip: The axon's fine endings are the telodendrites.
steps.margin_note: Name the telodendrites and say they reach many fibres.

lines.text: Its telodendrites reach all those fibres

insider_note: The answer needs both halves — the nerve cell AND the muscle fibres it reaches. Naming only the neuron is half an answer.
